Overview
Build at the frontier of agentic AI. August 28–31, 2026. Online, individual, free.
AI can produce convincing code in seconds. Real engineering begins when convincing is not enough: incomplete requirements, hidden dependencies, difficult edge cases, failure modes, and decisions that require technical judgment.

The micro1 Frontier Engineering Challenge is a free, global, online competition for engineers ready to work at that frontier. Over a three-day sprint you will use coding agents to tackle a real-world software engineering problem and produce a solution that is correct, reproducible, testable and clearly explained.

 

 

The full challenge statement is released at kickoff (Aug 28 at 15:00 UTC). Until then, expect to build at the frontier of agentic AI without details that would reveal the problem in advance.

Participants will be able to registre after the Hackathon kicks off. The Hackathon ends on Aug 31 at 18:00 UTC.

Participants are evaluated on the quality of the submitted work, not résumé prestige, job title, university, employer or geography.

Coding-agent use is required. You must disclose the tools you used and submit the required trajectories for evaluation.

 

 

About micro1
micro1 is the leading AI data lab for training frontier models and evaluating AI agents. Experts contribute their diverse subject matter knowledge across domains such as finance, healthcare, STEM engineering, and more. micro1 transforms that real-world expertise into high-quality training data, evaluations, and feedback loops that improve how AI systems learn, reason, and perform.

Our platform identifies and vets top talent through an AI recruiter, enabling high-quality expert contributions at scale. We aim to enable 1 billion people to do meaningful work by applying their expertise to AI. As our global expert network grows, micro1 is building the human intelligence layer for frontier AI.

 

 
Stay connected with Micro1 across our social channels for the latest updates, opportunities, and insights: LinkedIn | Instagram | X | Reddit | YouTube
 

Theme
Build at the frontier of agentic AI.
Use coding agents to tackle a real-world engineering problem where correctness, reproducibility and human judgment matter.

In short: let your creativity run. Show us how you think through code. Apply it to any industry you like.

 

 

The full problem PDF, starter materials, constraints and acceptance tests are published at kickoff.

Every valid entry must present both a baseline solution and an advanced solution. The advanced solution should show a meaningful improvement in capability, reliability, efficiency, coverage or engineering quality, not a cosmetic variation.

 

Technology policy
Supported languages include Python, TypeScript, Java, C++, Go and Rust. Commonly used frameworks and libraries in those ecosystems are allowed, provided the entry stays reproducible and complies with the final problem PDF.

Illustrative examples: FastAPI, Flask, Django, LangGraph and related Python ecosystems; Node.js, Express, NestJS and Next.js for TypeScript; Spring Boot for Java; standard C++ and CMake toolchains; Go modules and common Go web frameworks; and Cargo, Tokio, Axum or Actix for Rust. This list is intentionally non-exhaustive.

The problem PDF may prescribe a starter repository, runtime, dependency limits, API access or testing environment where needed for fair and deterministic judging.

Instruction
HACHATHON IS NOW LIVE! Feel free to access the instructions here: INSTRUCTIONS

Prizes & Awards
$10,000 in cash, three selective awards, and up to 50 paid opportunities.

 

 
Opportunities at micro1
Up to 50 top performers may be considered for paid, flexible engineering work with micro1, subject to technical verification, eligibility and project availability. Additional strong performers may be invited to complete micro1's accelerated AI interview. Every eligible participant with a valid submission receives a digital participation certificate.

 

If you're interested in taking a look at some of our openings, please see our most in demand engineering roles here:

 

Senior Software Engineer

Open Source Contributor

Senior Back End Engineer

 

Or browse our opportunities page here.

 

Conditional coding-agent reimbursement
After validation, micro1 may separately offer to acquire qualifying agent-use traces at $2 to $15 per trace, capped at $100 to $200 per participant. This is not part of the $10,000 prize pool, does not affect judging, and is not guaranteed by registering or submitting. Any acquisition runs under separate terms covering artifacts acquired, permitted uses, rights granted, compensation, validation standard, privacy treatment and payment timing.

Stages & Timeline
Plan. Build. Prove. Submit.

Eligibility Criteria
Participants must be at least 18 years old at the time of registration.
Open globally except where participation or payment is prohibited by applicable law, sanctions, export controls, or organizer and platform restrictions.
Entries are individual only. A participant may register once and submit one final entry. Revisions are allowed until the deadline; only the latest complete submission is evaluated.
Participants should have at least six months of practical software-building experience or equivalent hands-on evidence. Professional employment is not required.
Eligible participants include working engineers, founders, open-source contributors, competitive programmers, final-year students, graduate students and recent graduates who meet the experience standard.
micro1 employees, event administrators, judges, anyone involved in creating or testing the challenge, and their immediate household members are not eligible for prizes.
Participants must be able to receive payment through the approved payout rail in their country to receive a cash prize or trace-acquisition payment.
Accurate identity, location, contact and eligibility information is required. Duplicate or false registrations may be disqualified.
Evaluation Criteria
Scored out of 100 by micro1's engineering team.
Qualification gate. A submission is scored only after it passes eligibility, completeness, integrity, trace and reproducibility checks. A project that cannot be run or verified may be disqualified before rubric scoring.

 

Tie-break order
Higher Agent Solution & Engineering score
Higher Reproducibility score
Higher Measured Improvement score
Higher End to End Quality score
Final panel review of documented evidence. The judges' decision is binding to the extent permitted by law and the official terms
Submission Package

Complete solution code and improvement changelog
Share the full project and everything required to run it, including the instructions that shape each agent. Use the README to introduce the intended user, explain their current bottleneck, and describe why solving it is valuable. Add a clearly labelled Improvement Changelog with an entry for every meaningful iteration, connected to the evidence that guided your next decision. Close with the main failure mode and your hot take.

Reproduction guide. 
Written for someone starting from a clean environment. Walk them through setup and give the exact commands for the solution, the baseline and the evaluation. Explain which data is required and what output to expect. Share relevant versions along with approximate runtime and cost.

Solution video, up to 5 minutes. 
Begin with the problem and the simple baseline, then walk through one realistic execution from start to finish. Show the final comparison and briefly explain the changelog. Highlight the change that contributed most, and one experiment you removed.

Agent trajectories. 
Representative trajectories for every agent you used, easy to follow from the agent instructions through to the final result. Show what the agent did and how its tools responded. Capture the feedback that shaped its next step, plus any retries or human checkpoints.

Rule Book
You are welcome to build with tools and components you already know.

Make it clear what existed before the competition and what you added.

Use every tool and component according to its licence and service terms.

Keep consequential actions controlled through a sandbox or simulation. Add human approval before the action happens.

Make a qualified human reviewer part of any solution that could significantly affect someone.

Choose a legal and ethical use case that treats people and their data responsibly.

Use information you are allowed to share. Public or synthetic data are usually easiest. Approved anonymous data also works.

Keep credentials and private information outside the submission.

Connect every claim about your results to the evidence you submit.

Give judges enough access to run the project and reproduce the main result.

Submissions are governed by the Hackathon Participation Agreement (accepted at registration), under which micro1 owns submissions and may use them for AI model training and evaluation.

FAQs
Q: Is registration free?

A: Yes. There is no fee to register or submit.

 

Q: Can I participate as a team?

A: No. The August 2026 edition is for individual participation and individual prizes.

 

Q: When will the exact problem be available?

A: The exact problem will be revealed at kickoff on August 28th. Before then, micro1 will share the theme, rules, submission requirements, and schedule.

 

Q: Are AI tools allowed?

A: Yes. Coding-agent use is required. You must disclose the tools you use and submit the required trajectories or traces.

 

Q: Do you provide API keys or model credits?

A: No. Participants must use their own agent setup.

 

Q: Which programming languages can I use?

A: Any language is allowed, with Python, TypeScript, Java, C++, Go, and Rust recommended, subject to the runtime constraints in the final problem PDF.

 

Q: Do I need to be looking for a job to participate?

A: No. This is a competition. Any future interest in paid micro1 work will be handled separately.

 

Q: What makes a submission valid?

A: A valid submission must be timely, complete, original, policy compliant, and reproducible, and include the required repository, archive, tests, README, agent-use evidence, and demo video.

 

Q: Does every submission receive a certificate?

A: Yes. Every eligible participant with a valid submission receives a digital participation certificate.

 

Q: Does submitting guarantee trace reimbursement or a job?

A: No. Trace acquisition is a separate, limited programme if approved. Employment and project opportunities are separate and subject to additional review.

 

Q: How much time will this take?

A: Plan for a focused three-day weekend. Keep your problem scope tight so the deliverables are achievable within the timeframe.

 

Q: Where can I get help?

A: Use the organizer contact and Help options on the challenge page. Official clarifications will be shared with all participants.

Challenge is live

Start submission

What this actually is

What the field will submit

Will not place

Chatbots, RAG wrappers, AI todo apps, generic multi-agent demos, unfinished Next.js dashboards, solutions with no baseline, solutions with no eval, trajectories that are screenshots of ChatGPT, videos that never show a full run. One public weekend repo in this theme (abhie2005/FrontierHackathon) is a multi-agent logistics pipeline. That shape is closer than a chatbot, but complexity without a frozen verifier and a measured baseline delta will not beat a smaller, fully proven system.

Will place

A sharp user, a real bottleneck, a dumb baseline that actually runs, an advanced loop that beats it on a frozen eval, traces that show retries and human checkpoints, Docker or one-command setup, a 5-minute video that follows their script. Judges evaluate agents for a living (Cortex, Realm, expert traces). They will smell LLM-as-judge-only evals, reward hacking, and undocumented agent sessions immediately.

Build a sandboxed incomplete-spec workflow with a frozen verifier. Not another chatbot. This matches the theme, the rule book (sandbox + human approval before consequential actions), and what micro1 sells. Primary}> LedgerGate — invoice reconciliation under incomplete matching rules Intended user: an ops engineer at a small commerce company who currently reconciles invoices to payments in a spreadsheet and cannot tell whether an agent-generated matcher is safe to run. All on synthetic invoices with planted failure modes (partial pay, reversed wires, OCR-ish references, same-amount different vendors). Must stay synthetic and non-clinical. Strong only if the eval set is tight. One workflow, one eval harness, one sandbox ledger or service. content.text:
There are **no previous winners**. This is micro1’s first public hackathon. Copying last year’s project is not an option. Winning is a complete, reproducible, measured baseline-vs-advanced package with agent traces — not a flashy demo.

I put the scoring map, recommended build, and today’s hour plan in [win-the-challenge](/Users/eugenius/.cursor/projects/Users-eugenius-Life-Frontier-Engineering-Challenge-2026/canvases/win-the-challenge.canvas.tsx) so you can keep it open beside the chat. A canvas is a live view next to the conversation; I used it because the rubric, checklist, and timeline are easier to use that way than as a long markdown dump.

**Deadline is tonight: 18:00 UTC (21:00 Nairobi).** Your repo is still empty. Stop expanding ideas. Ship one tight system.

---

## What the challenge actually is

It is **not** a hidden LeetCode problem. The live theme is open-ended: pick a real engineering bottleneck in any industry, use coding agents, and submit **both a baseline and an advanced solution** with a meaningful, measured improvement.

micro1 is an AI data lab. They train and evaluate agents. They explicitly buy traces ($2–$15 each, optional, separate from prizes) and own submissions for model training. Judges are their engineers. They will score **judgment, traces, and reproducibility**, not résumé prestige.

Prize picture from organizer posts: **$10,000 pool, $5,000 first**, three selective awards, up to 50 paid gigs, certificate for every valid entry. ~8.3k registered. Typical hackathon submit rates are 5–15%, and many complete entries still fail the qualification gate.

**Do this first:** open the live **INSTRUCTIONS** link on HackerEarth. I could not fetch it while logged out. If that PDF names a starter repo, runtime, or acceptance tests, follow it exactly and ignore any open-ended idea that conflicts with it.

---

## How you actually get scored

A **qualification gate** runs first: eligibility, completeness, integrity, traces, reproducibility. If a judge cannot clone and run it, it is not scored.

Then /100 on four axes. Tie-break order (this is the ranking, even though the point-weight images did not copy out of the page):

1. **Agent Solution & Engineering** — technical judgment under incomplete requirements
2. **Reproducibility** — clean machine, pinned deps, exact commands
3. **Measured Improvement** — numbers vs baseline, not adjectives
4. **End to End Quality** — one realistic run, evidence-linked changelog, honest failure mode

Required package:

- Full code, agent instructions, README (user, bottleneck, why it matters), **Improvement Changelog**, main failure mode, hot take
- Reproduction guide (setup, baseline command, advanced command, eval command, data, expected output, versions, runtime, cost)
- Video ≤ 5 minutes, in **their** order: problem → baseline → one full run → comparison → changelog → biggest win → one killed experiment
- Agent trajectories for **every** agent: instructions → tools → tool results → the feedback that changed the next step → retries and human checkpoints

Hard rules that kill otherwise good work: individual only; disclose agents; sandbox consequential actions and require human approval; public/synthetic data only; no secrets; licenses respected; every claim tied to submitted evidence.

---

## What to build (with ~11 hours left)

Build **LedgerGate**: a sandboxed **invoice-to-payment reconciler** with incomplete matching rules.

- **User:** ops engineer who currently matches invoices in a spreadsheet and cannot trust an agent with money.
- **Bottleneck:** naive matching looks right and then double-pays, skips partial remittances, or matches the wrong vendor.
- **Baseline:** deterministic fuzzy match on amount + vendor. No idempotency, no human gate. It runs. It fails planted cases. That is the point.
- **Advanced:** a tool-using agent that parses, proposes a match with evidence, abstains when ambiguous, and **asks a human before posting** to a sandbox ledger. Same frozen eval.
- **Metrics that win Measured Improvement:** exact-match accuracy, false-pay rate, duplicate-pay rate, abstention quality, pass@3, tokens, wall time.

This hits the rubric: incomplete spec, hidden edge cases, failure modes, human-in-the-loop, synthetic data, traces, and a number that moved. It is also the kind of evaluation loop micro1’s product (Cortex / Realm) is built around.

Do **not** build a chatbot, a RAG wrapper, an AI todo app, or a multi-agent theatre piece with no frozen verifier. One public weekend repo in this theme is already a logistics multi-agent pipeline. Complexity without a measured delta will lose to a smaller system that a judge can run in ten minutes.

Backups only if INSTRUCTIONS forbids payments-shaped work: **IncidentFix** (repair a tiny service from an incomplete ticket) or **ClaimsCode** on fully synthetic charts.

---

## How you make a first-place attempt realistic

You cannot “guarantee” a win against 8.3k names. You **can** beat the field on the gate and on traces, which is where most people die.

1. Write the eval and planted failures **before** any agent writes product code. If deleting your error handling does not fail a test, you do not have coverage.
2. Pin Docker + lockfile on hour one, not at 20:00.
3. Only keep an advanced change that moves the scorecard. Changelog rows cite the delta. One experiment you **removed** is required by the video brief — that is scored judgment, not confession.
4. Export real trajectories (this Cursor session plus runtime JSONL). Screenshots of ChatGPT will not pass a trace check.
5. Record the video to their script. Do not improvise a product tour.
6. Submit by **19:30 Nairobi** so you have slack. Latest complete package is the only one judged.

If you want, I can start scaffolding LedgerGate in this repo now: eval harness, synthetic invoices, baseline matcher, and the advanced agent loop. Say go.
